feasible.reason: Parts (a)+(b) are technically sound, feasible on pq1 without any firmware/flash-budget cost (host tooling only), and are the load-bearing external leg of invariant #10 that today exists only as a bench-profile script. Repo evidence checks out: tools/verify_ship_state.py reads only option bytes (via `--optionbytes displ`) and sha256s named flash regions; it never reads FLASH_NSSR, OTP (0x0BFA_0000), UID (0x0BFA_0590) or DBGMCU_IDCODE despite the docstring; tools/ship-profiles/ holds only bench-rdp0-tzen.json plus a template; shared/src/lockdown.rs:281-290 has OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED=false so oem_locks_absent() fails closed and no firmware path writes OEM1/2KEYR (grep: zero hits in secure/ and shared/); docs/security/user-device-verification.md is "DESIGN, nothing implemented"; #249 and #595 are OPEN. Trezor's stm32u5/option_bytes.c:213-222 and :247-249 confirm the vendor precedent exactly as stated. Reading NSSR/OTP/UID/IDCODE/TAMP_BKP over SWD at RDP-0 with NRST held (debugger has secure access at RDP-0 even with TZEN=1) is possible with STM32_Programmer_CLI `-r32`/`--read` or a CMSIS-DAP probe via DAPjs/WebUSB, so the consumer-binary + WebUSB shape is realisable. However part (c)/(d) is internally inconsistent for the stated threat and the "unconditional on factory honesty" claim is overstated — see corrections. Cost/priority are not wildly wrong for (a)+(b) but (c) is mis-costed and mis-prioritised.
feasible.corrections: 1. (d) contradicts the threat. A baseline recorded by the buyer/verifier at receipt detects only tampering AFTER that baseline (evil-maid), never transit/reseller interdiction that happened before receipt. The only (c) element that addresses the stated threat is the per-BATCH PDN golden set "published by the project" — which is a project/factory-recorded reference and therefore IS conditional on project honesty and on the golden-set distribution channel. Rewrite: (a)+(b) are unconditional on factory honesty; (c) photo/glitter protects post-receipt only; (c) PDN against transit needs either a trusted golden set or cross-unit comparison of N units bought through independent channels. 2. UID/DBGMCU_IDCODE reads defend against the "swapped MCU + transplanted genuine SEs" threat only if there is an expected UID to compare against — that is the factory-recorded triple-UID binding (#249, OPEN, not started). Without it the UID read is informational; with it, the defence is conditional on the factory record. A trojaned/clone die that emulates SWD and IDCODE defeats (a) entirely and is unlikely to move the PDN signature measurably; state this as the accepted residual. 3. "Published expected-digest file per release" cannot cover OTP, UID or TAMP_BKP — they are per-unit. OTP in particular holds the factory-burned per-device transport master (secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs); at RDP-0 anyone with SWD can read it anyway (transport creds are replaced on first boot), but the WebUSB page must treat the dump as a secret — compare locally, never upload or log it. The only release-level OTP check is a programmed-word MAP (which words/regions are 0xFF vs programmed), not a digest. 4. OEM-key closure is device-side, not verifier-side: OEM2KEY can be programmed at RDP-1, so the planting window includes the self-lock sequence itself. Mirror Trezor: write OEM1KEYR1/2 and OEM2KEYR1/2 = 0xFFFFFFFF in the same OPTSTRT as RDP=0xCC in first_boot Phase A (currently the firmware only halts with E080A; no overwrite exists). The external NSSR read detects a planted key; the overwrite neutralises it. Both still need the bench pin on a sacrificial board (lockdown.rs:281-290, #46/#387) or the check is vacuous (fail-closed today, so it halts every first boot). 5. SWD pad access is a blocking hardware precondition, not a "risk": evt-silicon-validation.md:661 records that the enclosed V10 unit has the 10-pin connector removed and pads inside the case (DFU via SBU/A8 only), while hardware_requirements.md:166 mandates SWD+NRST pads accessible after assembly. Without SWDIO/SWCLK/NRST/GND/VTref reachable on the SEALED unit, (a)+(b) collapse to "open the case", and the DFU/ROM-bootloader route is NOT an acceptable substitute (ROM bootloader is non-secure under TZEN=1 and reads the secure bank as zeros; it also runs code). Kind=mixed is right; make the pad decision explicit. 6. "Before first power" is physically imprecise — SWD needs VDD; the actual guarantee is NRST asserted (connect-under-reset) so no instruction executes. Say so, and note that powering the board floats PA8 (LDO2_EN) at reset, so the SE rail state during verification is pull-defined, not firmware-defined. 7. TAMP_BKP "expected erased" is weak on pq1: the backup domain is a 0.47–1 F supercap (hardware_requirements.md:139-150), which holds state for hours-to-days, not weeks; planted BKP state drains in transit and genuine units may show stale state if recently powered. Qualify as advisory. 8. PDN tier: the SE rail VDD1_3V3 sits behind LDO2 gated by PA8, so a VNA on the main PDN cannot see an implant on the SE rail — needs a probe point on that rail (hardware), plus exposed VDD/GND pads for a 2-port shunt-through fixture, and opening the case. PDNPulse's 100%/0% figures were on four boards in a lab with same-design references; a per-batch golden set across MLCC ±20% tolerance and DC-bias variance is unvalidated — classify as research/bench tier, not consumer. 9. Unflagged bypass for (a): a SWD interposer implant on PA13/PA14 (or in the buyer's own probe) can present clean flash; (c) only catches it if it is PDN-powered. Raises cost, does not prevent. 10. Cost/priority: (a)+(b) = M and correctly P0 (one profile JSON, ~5 extra register/memory reads, a static WebUSB page); (c) = L plus ongoing per-batch labour and ≥ $1k VNA, priority P2. Also the ship profile cannot be finalised until WRP1A/B and SECWM values for the 40 KiB FSBL cutover (#540) are decided — the profile would otherwise pin the legacy 32 KiB layout.

vendor-claim.reason: The precedent claims check out against the Trezor source and the vendor pages, and the novelty='beyond' claim survives: no wallet vendor (Trezor, Ledger, Coldcard, BitBox02, Blockstream Jade, Foundation Passport) ships a user-run pre-power flash/option-byte verifier; every one of them does post-power SE attestation or on-device self-check, and the two anti-interdiction precedents (Purism, Star Labs) are laptop vendors whose baselines are taken by the factory, not an independent verifier. The repo evidence is accurate in substance (verify_ship_state.py reads no OTP/UID/NSSR, lockdown OEM predicate fails closed because OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED=false, user-device-verification.md is unimplemented DESIGN, all cited issues are OPEN). The claim is incomplete rather than false: several line citations are off, the PDNPulse rationale conflates two experiments and overstates sensitivity, one cited source is a different paper, and the Trezor precedent is itself an on-device post-power check, i.e. not a precedent for the pre-power part of the proposal.
vendor-claim.corrections: (1) Trezor line citation: the OEM-key reset is core/embed/sec/option_bytes/stm32u5/option_bytes.c:213-222 (not :210-222; :209-211 are WRP1BR/WRP2AR/WRP2BR). The comment at :216-218 states the keys are write-only and OEMxLOCK in FLASH->NSSR is the only way to check. The write happens only inside flash_set_option_bytes(), i.e. when option bytes mismatched (boardloader main.c:325 -> option_bytes_configure :252-264), not on every boot. The every-boot check is option_bytes_check_oem_keys() :247-250 (ensure OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK clear), called from projects/kernel/main.c:181 and projects/secmon/main.c:123 under USE_OEM_KEYS_CHECK, which core/embed/models/build.rs:276,296,318,337 enables for the STM32U5 models T3W1/T3T1/T3T2/T3B1 only. Trezor tree at 6ab39e95 (2026-09-18). (2) Category correction: Trezor's OEM check is on-device, post-power self-verification — exactly the class tools/verify_ship_state.py:10-16 says is 'worth zero against interdiction'. It is precedent for the OEM-lock predicate (already mirrored in shared/src/lockdown.rs:264-290 and fsbl/src/optbytes.rs:22-28), not for pre-power external verification. (3) Omitted Trezor precedent: Trezor ships devices WITHOUT firmware and tells users 'If firmware is already installed the device should not be used' (trezor.io support page) — a supply-chain signal adjacent to this proposal; Suite signature check happens at connection, post-power. No SWD/pre-power procedure exists in Trezor docs (docs/ grep: only embed_debug/systemview mention SWD). (4) Omitted Coldcard precedent: Coinkite's security page says the SE checks flash against its recorded checksum at every boot (GENUINE/CAUTION light); the 'bag number shown on first boot + stored in OTP' detail comes from a secondary podcast source, Coinkite's own page only says 'bag number shown by the device'. (5) Ledger: Donjon threat-model page confirms SE attestation challenge-response at first connection, explicit rejection of tamper seals, and no pre-power verification. BitBox02/Jade/Passport: SE attestation at setup, post-power. (6) Purism: glitter on screws + interior photos, signed by Purism and GPG-encrypted out-of-band — baseline taken by the FACTORY (Purism), so proposal rule (d) is genuinely beyond it; Purism also states it does not claim to prevent interdiction. Star Labs: serialised seals + 'physical varnish markings' + verification photos sent before dispatch; glitter and firmware hashes are not mentioned on the page. (7) PDNPulse (arXiv 2204.02482 = IEEE TIFS 2023, DOI 10.1109/TIFS.2023.3285490) confirms 300 kHz-3 GHz (paper text line 465) and 2-port shunt-through (line 412). But '100% TPR / 0% FPR on four boards with multi-port probing' conflates two experiments: the 4-board result is the custom PoC board measured with ONE port (lines 983-993); the multi-port (3-/5-port) 100%/0% result is on 10 PYNQ FPGA boards (lines 1082, 1139). 'Sub-ohm sensitivity' is not supported as stated: the always-on Trojan detected is a 1 Ω sampling resistor (lines 890, 925, 990); the paper says 'minuscule' qualitatively. The per-batch caveat IS supported: Elegoo-I vs Elegoo-II batches with identical layout are distinguishable by impedance (lines 1329-1341) and the paper recommends multi-class FD-KNN. (8) Source mislabel: cyan.engineering.osu.edu/.../vlsi.pdf is Harrison/Asadizanjani/Tehranipoor (UF FICS), 'On Malicious Implants in PCBs throughout the Supply Chain' — a taxonomy paper supporting the threat model, NOT PDNPulse evidence. (9) Repo-evidence line fixes: tools/verify_ship_state.py:112-114 is the --mode UR argument, not a 'bench profile default'; the profile is a required positional (:109) and the only checkable profile is tools/ship-profiles/bench-rdp0-tzen.json (ship-option-b.template.json refuses via PENDING, :121-127). Option-byte parsing is a generic regex over programmer output (:86-89); neither profile names OEM/NSSR/OTP/UID keys; flash compare is :146-153. OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED=false is at shared/src/lockdown.rs:290, oem_locks_absent fails closed at :514; WRP1A_MASK_PINNED=false at :445. DBGMCU_IDCODE is already decoded in-firmware (secure/src/die_id.rs, secure/src/hw/dbgmcu.rs) but not by any external tool. (10) Risk-field confirmations: docs do disagree — docs/security/user-device-verification.md:184 wants SWD on SBU1/SBU2; docs/hardware/evt-debug-pins.md:150-152 shows V10's SBU1/SBU2 are ONE net driving a BOOT0 LDO enable (and :161 SWD pads remain on MP); docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:166-168 requires accessible SWD+NRST pads. VBAT is a direct contradiction, not an 'if populated': user-device-verification.md:190 requires 'No VBAT retention' while hardware_requirements.md:139-149 specifies a 0.47-1 F supercap keeping TAMP backup registers (BHK) alive — 'expected erased' backup registers cannot hold on that board. (11) Issues #249 (NOT STARTED), #68, #67 (ship-blocker), #595, #46, #270, #387 are all OPEN as claimed.
